rationale: The assistant correctly put up a stop-use warning from the outset, asked the right first question (new/cleaned vs electrical/plastic smell), used the customer's answers faithfully and escalated to an engineer without inventing anything or pushing parts. It was somewhat over-confident in stating 'The most likely cause is the mains terminal block' when the ground truth is genuinely uncertain between the supply connection/cooker switch and internal wiring, and it never probed the cooker switch, flickering or crackling, so it missed the supply-side hazard and the need for an electrician. The second turn also framed isolation at the fuse box as something the engineer would do rather than reiterating that the customer should isolate at the consumer unit now, though turn one had already told them to switch off at the fuse box.
